territorial_scope.description: Applies within Alabama as a state statute covering federal, state and local elections held in the state.

evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA:

summary.short: Alabama HB 172 makes it a crime to distribute materially deceptive media, meaning AI-produced images, audio or video that falsely depict an individual, within 90 days before an election when the distributor knows the media is false and intends to influence the election. It also lets specified parties seek permanent injunctions. Effective October 1, 2024.
summary.long: Alabama HB 172 makes it a crime to distribute materially deceptive media, meaning AI-produced images, audio or video that falsely depict an individual saying or doing something they did not, when a reasonable viewer would incorrectly believe it. Distribution is prohibited within 90 days before an election when the distributor knows the media falsely represents the depicted individual and intends, with reasonable likelihood, to harm a candidate's reputation or prospects or to change voters' patterns by deception. A disclaimer stating the media was manipulated by technical means and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur avoids the prohibition, with specific placement and language rules for video, audio, image and edited media. A violation is a Class A misdemeanor, but a second or subsequent conviction within five years is a Class D felony. Websites, interactive services, broadcasters and publishers are excluded absent actual knowledge and intent to injure or influence, and satire, qualifying news coverage and rights under federal law are carved out. Distributors may not intentionally remove a disclaimer. The Attorney General, depicted individuals, injured candidates and entities representing likely-deceived voters may seek permanent injunctive relief, must prove knowledge by clear and convincing evidence, and face dismissal and possible fees for frivolous complaints; non-Attorney General plaintiffs may recover costs and fees. The act takes effect October 1, 2024.

notes: The document is the bill text; it contains no enactment history or session-law record, so the adopted status comes from registry metadata only. Sec. 5 gives an effective date of October 1, 2024. Sec. 2(a) requires all four listed conditions, and Sec. 2(b) and 2(d) set out disclaimer and distributor exceptions tied to knowledge and intent. Sec. 2(c) states offence classes only, with no penalty amounts. Sec. 3 creates civil injunctive relief alongside the criminal offence in Sec. 2. Sec. 3 names several plaintiffs (depicted individual, candidate, representative entity), but these are classes of persons rather than named bodies, so only the Attorney General is coded as an entity. The FCC is referenced only in a savings clause and is not coded as an entity. Section_status is populated for schema compliance; relations and entities both contain entries.

obligations.summary: Prohibits a person from distributing, or agreeing with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media when the person knows it falsely represents a depicted individual, the distribution occurs within 90 days before an election, and the person intends harm to a candidate or a change in voting patterns that is reasonably likely to result. Does not apply where the Sec. 2(b) disclaimer conditions are met.
obligations.conditional_on: Distribution within 90 days before an election; knowledge of falsity; specified intent and reasonable likelihood; and the Sec. 2(b) exception not met.

evidence.quote: a person shall not distribute, or enter into an agreement with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media if all of the following apply

obligations.summary: Creator, sponsor or purchaser must include a disclaimer in any presentation of the media stating that it has been manipulated by technical means and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur, as a condition of the Sec. 2(a) exception. Sec. 2(b)(2)-(5) add format requirements for video, audio-only, image and edited media, including a citation to the original source for media generated by editing existing content.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies only where the creator, sponsor or purchaser seeks to rely on the exception in Sec. 2(b) to the Sec. 2(a) prohibition.

evidence.quote: The creator, sponsor, or purchaser includes a disclaimer in any presentation of the media informing the viewer both that the media has been manipulated by technical means and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur.

obligations.summary: A distributor must not intentionally remove a disclaimer included with media by the creator, sponsor or purchaser.
obligations.conditional_on: A disclaimer has been included with the media by the creator, sponsor or purchaser.

evidence.quote: A distributor shall not intentionally remove a disclaimer included with any media by the creator, sponsor, or purchaser of the media.
